title: Dictator versus low influence tester
statement: A randomized sign tester distinguishes dictators from Boolean functions with no influential coordinate using a finite allowed predicate family if that family is finite, $0<\alpha<\beta\le 1$, and the error function takes values in $[0,1]$ on $[0,1]$ and tends to $0$ as its positive argument tends to $0$. For every positive input dimension, the tester uses only predicates from that family and accepts every dictator with probability at least $\beta$. For every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, it accepts each function whose coordinate influences are all at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at most $\alpha+\mathrm{error}(\varepsilon)$.
hypotheses_covered: Error tends to zero as the positive argument tends to zero
